condition_8_labels.note: export-metrics.py queries are namespace-wide by design (matches every prior successful run, e.g. block6) -- edge-tier/edge-deployment labels are expected to co-occur, not a defect. Presence (not exclusivity) of workload-cloud/tier=cloud is the correct check.

pod_lifecycle_cross_check.explanation: cpu_cores uses rate(...[1m]); a pod alive for well under 1 minute (e.g. a brief agent scale-up/down blip) can be captured by the pod-lifecycle poller but produce no rate() sample. This is an expected Prometheus rate-window artifact, not evidence of a data gap.

condition_9_source: all rows written directly from live Prometheus query_range HTTP responses via unmodified export-metrics.py; no manual/interpolated/constant values

workload_pod_violations_check.source: existing pod_lifecycle.jsonl from the original run, LifecycleTracker.check_validity() unmodified

agent_policy_match_check.note: Not re-derivable now (orchestration-agent is scaled to 0 as part of clean-baseline restoration; live re-query would reflect current state, not the state during the run). The original runs own execution log already recorded "Selecting policy policies/ablation_g30.yaml" / "Arm G30 (guarded predictive, cooldown 30s) active" before k6 started, matching qc_checks.EXPECTED_AGENT_POLICY["G30"]. Not independently re-verified via a fresh kubectl query in this recovery pass.
